items.stem: A RAG system filters out restricted documents only after they are placed in the prompt. Why is this unsafe?

options.text: The restricted content has already entered the context and can leak into the answer
options.rationale: Correct: once in context, restricted text can surface; filter before retrieval.

options.text: Post-filtering is faster but always correct
options.rationale: It is not correct; the data is already exposed.

options.text: The model encrypts restricted text automatically

options.rationale: Order is exactly what matters here.

items.explanation: Correct: once in context, restricted text can surface; filter before retrieval.

items.stem: Which TWO are required for permission-aware retrieval? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Access metadata attached to documents at index time
options.rationale: Correct: filtering needs permission metadata on documents.

options.text: Propagating the calling user's identity to the retrieval query
options.rationale: Correct: the query must know who is asking.

options.text: Using one shared service identity for every user
Raising the number of retrieved chunks
options.rationale: Chunk count does not enforce access.

items.explanation: Correct: filtering needs permission metadata on documents.

items.stem: Before launch, what best demonstrates that access control works?

options.text: Negative tests proving a user cannot retrieve documents they lack permission for
options.rationale: Correct: negative access tests prove enforcement.

options.text: A demo where an admin sees everything
options.rationale: Admin access does not test restriction.
Latency is unrelated to access correctness.
Model size does not enforce access.

items.explanation: Correct: negative access tests prove enforcement.
